options_evaluated: Monolithic recycled polymer housing with integrated structural ribs
assessments.recommendation: Monolithic recycled polymer housing with integrated structural ribs
assessments.rationale: This option maximizes the use of recycled materials (parameter h) and reduces the material footprint (parameter o) in line with Page 2, which emphasizes 'reducing its carbon footprint and material footprint... [using] secondary raw materials'. By utilizing integrated structural ribs, it achieves lightweight design (parameter t) through 'load- and stress-optimisation of structures' and 'integration of functions within the material or into a single product component' (Page 80). Avoiding co-molded rubber elements ensures that the housing does not contain composite mixtures that 'make the reuse, or recycling process more complicated, costly, environmentally impactful, or energy- or resource-demanding' (Page 35, Article 2(27)(d)).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use stage, where users may prefer co-molded rubber grips for ergonomic comfort and vibration dampening, and the Manufacturing stage, which may find monolithic structures with complex internal ribbing harder to eject from molds.

options_evaluated: Threaded metal fasteners into brass inserts
assessments.recommendation: Threaded metal fasteners into brass inserts
assessments.rationale: This method directly supports 'ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly' (Page 79, parameters b and c), which is vital for component recovery and repair. Avoiding chemical adhesives or permanent ultrasonic welds ensures that different material fractions (plastics and metals) can be cleanly separated, preventing the introduction of substances that 'impair the technical properties or functionalities... of the recycled material' (Page 35, Article 2(27)(b)) and facilitating high-quality 'design for recycling' (parameter d).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing stage, which favors ultrasonic welding or snap-fits for lower assembly cycle times and reduced bill-of-materials cost, and the Lightweight design stage (parameter t), as metal fasteners add slight weight and volume (parameter j).

options_evaluated: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with glueless, mechanically retained magnets
Brushed DC motor with glued permanent magnets
assessments.recommendation: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with glueless, mechanically retained magnets
assessments.rationale: A BLDC motor with mechanically retained magnets supports 'ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly' (Page 79, parameter b), allowing the high-value magnets and copper windings to be separated at end-of-life. Avoiding chemical glues prevents contamination of the metallic fractions, ensuring that substances do not 'make the reuse, or recycling process more complicated' (Page 35). This design prioritizes 'the possibility for the recovery of materials' (Page 33) and reduces the product's overall material footprint (parameter o, Page 2).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing stage due to the increased complexity of designing and assembling mechanical retention clips for magnets compared to simple gluing.

options_evaluated: Passive heat dissipation via an integrated recycled aluminum heat sink
Active fan cooling with a separate plastic impeller
assessments.recommendation: Passive heat dissipation via an integrated recycled aluminum heat sink
assessments.rationale: Passive cooling using recycled aluminum integrates thermal management directly into the structural frame of the tool, fulfilling the lightweight design parameter (parameter t) through 'integration of functions within the material or into a single product component' (Page 80). It also incorporates recycled materials (parameter h) and avoids complex chemical phase-change materials that could act as 'substances of concern' (parameter f, Page 9) or complicate the recycling process at end-of-life (Page 35).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use stage, as passive cooling may result in higher external housing temperatures during prolonged operation, potentially impacting user comfort.

options_evaluated: Modular cartridge-based architecture with separate, pluggable modules
assessments.recommendation: Modular cartridge-based architecture with separate, pluggable modules
assessments.rationale: This architecture directly addresses 'ease of repair and maintenance' and 'ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing and refurbishment' (Page 79, parameters b and c) by utilizing 'standard components' and ensuring 'ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly' without specialized tools. It avoids potting compounds, which act as substances of concern that 'make the reuse, or recycling process more complicated, costly, [or] environmentally impactful' (Page 35).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with 'lightweight design' (parameter t, Page 80) and 'weight and volume of the product' (parameter j, Page 80), as modular connectors and separate cartridge housings add physical bulk and mass compared to a single integrated board.

options_evaluated: Removable, standardized slide-on battery pack with fastener-assembled cells
assessments.recommendation: Removable, standardized slide-on battery pack with fastener-assembled cells
assessments.rationale: A removable battery pack utilizing 'standard components' (Page 79, parameter c) and assembled with mechanical fasteners rather than glue ensures 'ease of non-destructive disassembly' (Page 79, parameter b). This facilitates the replacement, refurbishment, and eventual 'decontamination and recovery' of the battery cells when they become waste (Page 9). It prevents battery chemicals from contaminating the rest of the tool, supporting 'design for recycling' (parameter d) and reducing the Union's dependency on critical raw materials (Page 2).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with 'lightweight design' (parameter t, Page 80) and 'weight and volume' (parameter j, Page 80), as a slide-on pack requires a dedicated plastic enclosure and heavy contact interfaces compared to an integrated pouch cell.
